mainTopic: An אריס's duties: replanting, the planting season, disaster discounts, paying rent from the field's crop, and switching crops
overview: This amud opens by closing an earlier challenge with קשיא, which means it stays unanswered. Two ברייתות disagree on how many times an אריס must replant a ruined field. The גמרא explains that they follow רבי (a חזקה is set after two times) and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל (three times). ריש לקיש limits this to crops that sprouted and were eaten by locusts. If nothing sprouted, the farmer keeps planting all season, which רב פפא says ends when כימה is overhead. A ברייתא listing six seasons seems to contradict רב פפא, and the גמרא answers that he is talking about late crops. Next, רבא gives a money renter a discount for a מכת מדינה and sets aside רבי יהודה's opposite view. A new משנה teaches that wheat rent is paid from the field's own wheat. The גמרא limits this to cases where the land itself failed at its job. A final משנה forbids switching to a crop that is harder on the field, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל forbids any switch. רב חסדא bases that view on keeping one's word, and a challenge from the פורים collection begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The earlier challenge stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends the previous discussion: the claim 'I was worthy' remains a problem with no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'I was worthy'? This is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge from the previous discussion, which turned on the claim 'I was worthy.' It admits that this challenge has no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word קשיא here means the problem is left standing; no answer is given. It closes that thread so the גמרא can move on to a new topic.

keyTerms.meaning: I was worthy, meaning I was deserving of good fortune
It is difficult; the question stays unanswered

steps.confusionAlert: When the word קשיא stands alone at the end of a discussion, it does not open a new question. It means the earlier challenge was never resolved.

phrases.english: 'I was worthy'?
phrases.notes: This picks up a word from the earlier discussion, where someone claimed 'I was deserving.'

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge from the previous section of the daf
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The challenge based on 'I was worthy' is left unresolved.

steps.title: Two teachings disagree on how many times to replant
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא says the farmer replants twice and stops at the third time. Another says he replants a third time and stops only at the fourth.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא teaches: the first and second time, he plants it again, but the third time he does not have to. Another ברייתא teaches: the third time he plants it again, but the fourth time he does not have to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets two ברייתות side by side, and they seem to contradict each other about how many times a farmer must replant a field after the crops were destroyed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sources agree that at some point the farmer stops replanting. They disagree only on when that point comes: after two losses or after three. That one-time difference is the contradiction the גמרא needs to explain.

phrases.english: It is taught in one [ברייתא]:
The first and second time, he plants it,
but the third time, he does not plant it.
And it is taught in another [ברייתא]:
The third time, he plants it;
the fourth time, he does not plant it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the previous challenge was closed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One source says the farmer stops after two losses, and the other says he stops after three. Both cannot be right unless something separates them.

steps.title: Each teaching follows a different תנא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that one ברייתא follows רבי and the other follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this one follows רבי, and that one follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by assigning each ברייתא to a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two ברייתות are not really clashing. They reflect a known disagreement between two תנאים. The next step explains what that disagreement is.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no real contradiction
This one follows one view, and that one follows another

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is according to רבי,
that one is according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא כְּרַבִּי, הָא כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the two sources to two different תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two ברייתות stating different numbers must contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each ברייתא follows a different תנא, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: Two times or three times to make a pattern
steps.stepSummary: רבי holds that a חזקה is set after two times, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds it is set after three.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one follows רבי, who says a חזקה is made by two times. That one follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who says a חזקה is made by three times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind its answer. The two תנאים disagree about how many repeated events it takes to set an established pattern (חזקה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the crops have been destroyed enough times to form a חזקה, we assume this field is just going to keep failing, so the farmer does not have to replant. For רבי, that pattern is set after two losses, so he stops at the third. For רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, it takes three losses, so he stops at the fourth.

keyTerms.meaning: An established pattern or presumption created by something repeating

steps.whatToRemember: The number of replantings depends on the disagreement over חזקה: two times according to רבי, and three times according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whyThisMatters: The disagreement between רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל about how many times make a חזקה shows up in many places across ש״ס. Here it is applied to a farming case.

phrases.english: This one is according to רבי, who says:
By two times, it is a presumption.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the letter in square brackets and some don't. Either way, the word means 'it is.'

phrases.aramaic: הָא כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, דְּאָמַר:
phrases.english: That one is according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who says:
By three times, it is a presumption.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא כְּרַבִּי, דְּאָמַר: בִּתְרֵי זִימְנֵי הָוְיָא חֲזָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the answer in step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ties each number to a known view about חזקה
steps.terutzMaskana: The farmer replants until the destruction becomes a חזקה: two times for רבי, three times for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: The limit applies only when crops sprouted and were eaten
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the limit on replanting applies only when the crops sprouted and locusts ate them. If nothing sprouted, the owner can make the farmer keep planting all season.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: They taught this only when he planted it, it sprouted, and locusts ate it. But if he planted it and it did not sprout, the owner of the land can tell him: Keep on planting it for all the days of the planting season.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש narrows the rule from the ברייתות. It only covers a case where the plants grew and were then destroyed by locusts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the crops sprouted and then locusts came, the field showed it can grow, and the loss came from outside. When nothing sprouts at all, the owner can demand that the farmer keep trying for as long as it is still planting season. The limit of two or three times does not apply in that case.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of

steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש does not reject the ברייתות. He limits them to one kind of loss: the crops sprouted and then were eaten.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
They taught this only
where he planted it, and it sprouted, and locusts ate it.
But if he planted it and it did not sprout,
the owner of the land can say to him:
All the days of planting,
keep on planting it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the replanting rule from the ברייתות
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The limit on replanting applies only when the crops sprouted and were eaten by locusts. If they never sprouted, the farmer must keep planting for the whole season.

steps.title: When does the planting season end
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how long the planting season lasts.
steps.simpleTranslation: And until when?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the end point of the planting season that ריש לקיש just mentioned. This sets up רב פפא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'all the days of planting' needs a clear end date. Otherwise, we would not know when the farmer may stop.

phrases.english: And until when?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of 'all the days of planting' from step 5

steps.title: Until the Pleiades stand overhead
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the season lasts until the farmers come in from the field and the star group כימה is right above their heads.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Until the sharecroppers come in from the field and the כימה stars stand over their heads.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers with a sign from nature: the season ends when the כימה stars are overhead as the farmers return home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses a star sign that farmers would know, so the end of the season is easy to recognize. Once that time comes, the farmer no longer has to replant a field that did not sprout.

keyTerms.meaning: Sharecroppers, the tenant farmers who work for a share of the crop
The Pleiades, a group of stars

steps.whatToRemember: If the crops sprouted and were then eaten, the farmer replants two or three times (depending on חזקה). If they never sprouted, he keeps planting until the planting season ends, which is when כימה stands overhead.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Until the sharecroppers come in from the field
and the Pleiades stand over their heads.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: עַד דְּאָתוּ אֲרִיסֵי מִדַּבְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 6
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The planting season lasts until the sharecroppers return from the field with the כימה stars overhead.

steps.title: A ברייתא divides the year into six seasons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא, from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the name of רבי מאיר, that divides the year into six two-month seasons. Planting season runs from mid-תשרי to mid-כסלו.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said in the name of רבי מאיר, and רבי שמעון בן מנסיא said the same: second half of תשרי, all of מרחשון, first half of כסלו is planting time. Second half of כסלו, טבת, first half of שבט is winter. Second half of שבט, אדר, first half of ניסן is cold. Second half of ניסן, אייר, first half of סיון is harvest. Second half of סיון, תמוז, first half of אב is summer. Second half of אב, אלול, first half of תשרי is heat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a challenge to רב פפא by quoting a ברייתא that splits the year into six seasons. This step sets up the challenge; the actual question comes a little later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this ברייתא, planting season ends in the middle of כסלו. Keep that date in mind, because the גמרא will compare it to רב פפא's much later time limit.
steps.confusionAlert: Each season is two months long, but it starts and ends in the MIDDLE of a month, not at the start of one.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר,
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says in the name of Rabbi Meir,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן מְנַסְיָא אוֹמֵר כִּדְבָרָיו:
phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya would also say like his words:

phrases.aramaic: חֲצִי תִשְׁרֵי, מְרַחְשְׁוָן, וַחֲצִי כִסְלֵיו – זֶרַע.
phrases.english: Half of Tishrei, Marcheshvan, and half of Kislev: planting.
phrases.notes: The six season names come from the פסוק in בראשית 8:22.

phrases.aramaic: חֲצִי כִסְלֵיו, טֵבֵת, וַחֲצִי שְׁבָט – חוֹרֶף.
phrases.english: Half of Kislev, Tevet, and half of Shevat: winter.

phrases.aramaic: חֲצִי שְׁבָט, אֲדָר, וַחֲצִי נִיסָן – קוֹר.
phrases.english: Half of Shevat, Adar, and half of Nisan: cold.

phrases.aramaic: חֲצִי נִיסָן, אִיָּיר, וַחֲצִי סִיוָן – קָצִיר.
phrases.english: Half of Nisan, Iyar, and half of Sivan: harvest.

phrases.aramaic: חֲצִי סִיוָן, תַּמּוּז, וַחֲצִי אָב – קַיִץ.
phrases.english: Half of Sivan, Tammuz, and half of Av: summer.

phrases.aramaic: חֲצִי אָב, אֱלוּל, וַחֲצִי תִּשְׁרֵי – חוֹם.
phrases.english: Half of Av, Elul, and half of Tishrei: heat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to challenge רב פפא's definition of the planting season from Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's statement that planting season lasts until כימה is overhead
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup: the ברייתא sets planting season as ending in mid-כסלו, which is earlier than רב פפא's limit.

steps.title: Other opinions on when the seasons start
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that רבי יהודה starts counting the seasons from תשרי, and רבי שמעון starts from מרחשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה counts from תשרי. רבי שמעון counts from מרחשון.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going and gives two other opinions about where the six seasons begin. This sets up the גמרא's question about who is the most lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, planting season is all of תשרי and מרחשון. For רבי שמעון, it is מרחשון and כסלו, so his planting season ends the latest, at the end of כסלו.

keyTerms.meaning: Counts (starts the count of the seasons)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda counts from Tishrei,
Rabbi Shimon counts from Marcheshvan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with other opinions on when the count starts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה starts the seasons at the beginning of תשרי; רבי שמעון starts them at מרחשון.

steps.title: Even the most lenient view ends planting before רב פפא's time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רבי שמעון has the latest planting season, and even he does not stretch it as late as רב פפא does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the most lenient of all of them? רבי שמעון. And even he did not say it goes that far!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא states its actual challenge against רב פפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Of all the opinions, רבי שמעון's planting season ends the latest, at the end of כסלו. Even so, רב פפא's time of כימה being overhead is later than that, so רב פפא seems to go against every opinion in the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Is lenient (here: makes the planting season last the longest)

phrases.english: Who is the most lenient of all of them? Rabbi Shimon,
phrases.notes: Lenient here means his planting season ends the latest.

phrases.english: and even he did not say it goes that far!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא from Steps 8 and 9 to attack רב פפא in Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's time limit for planting season (Step 7)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No opinion in the ברייתא has planting season last as late as רב פפא says, not even the most lenient one, רבי שמעון.

steps.title: Early crops and late crops
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about early crops, while רב פפא is talking about a farmer who took on planting late crops.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one is where he took it on for early crops, and that one is where he took it on for late crops.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that the ברייתא and רב פפא are talking about two different kinds of planting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's seasons describe the normal planting time for early crops. רב פפא is talking about a farmer who agreed to plant late crops, which are planted much later, so his season really does run longer. The two sources do not argue.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
He took it on (the farmer accepted the field to plant)

steps.whatToRemember: How long a farmer must keep replanting depends on which crop he agreed to plant: early crops have a short season, and late crops have a longer one, all the way until כימה is overhead.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is where he took it on from him for early crops,
phrases.notes: This first "this" is the ברייתא with its six seasons.

phrases.english: that is where he took it on from him for late crops.
phrases.notes: This second "that" is רב פפא's longer season.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source is talking about a different kind of crop
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Planting season is one fixed period for all crops, so רב פפא seems to go against the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is talking about early crops; רב פפא is talking about a farmer who took on late crops, whose season lasts longer.

steps.title: Quoting רבי יהודה's view on renting for money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: רבי יהודה's opinion about a renter who agreed to pay money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: if the renter took the field from the owner for money (rather than for crops), the rule is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה to set up the story that comes next. It is opening the topic, not ruling yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the משנה taught that in a מכת מדינה the renter may take a discount off his rent. רבי יהודה adds that if the rent was set in money, the renter never gets a discount. The full wording of his view appears in step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: He received it, meaning he took the field to work it
Money (as opposed to payment in crops)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
If he received it from him for money.
phrases.notes: This is only the opening words. The full line, that he gets no discount either way, is quoted in step 15.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אִם קִבְּלָה מִמֶּנּוּ בְּמָעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the discussion of planting seasons to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, a renter who pays a fixed money rent is treated differently and gets no discount for a disaster.

steps.title: The case of the garlic field by the river
steps.stepSummary: A man rented land by the river מלכא סבא for money to grow garlic, and the river became blocked.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man rented land on the bank of the old royal river to grow garlic, and he paid in money (זוזים). Then the river got dammed up, so the field could not be watered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life case. It is setting up the ruling that רבא will give in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two details matter here. The rent was money, which is exactly רבי יהודה's case. And the damage came from the river being blocked, which may count as a מכת מדינה.

phrases.english: A certain man who received land
to plant garlic in it
on the bank of the river Malka Sava, for money.
The river Malka Sava became dammed up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a practical case that fits the money-rent situation of רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A case is presented: land rented for money, and the crop was ruined because the river was blocked.

steps.title: רבא rules it is a regional disaster and allows a discount
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the river does not normally get blocked, so this counts as a מכת מדינה, and the renter may lower his rent.
steps.simpleTranslation: The man came before רבא. רבא told him: this river does not usually get blocked, so this is a regional disaster. Go and take the loss off the rent you owe the owner.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his ruling: because the damage was unusual, it counts as a מכת מדינה, and the renter gets a discount even though he pays money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's reasoning is that an unusual event that the renter could not have expected counts as a regional disaster. By giving a discount on a money rent, he is going against רבי יהודה. That is what sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A regional disaster that strikes the whole area
Go, subtract it for him (take it off the rent)

phrases.english: He came before Rava.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: נְהַר מַלְכָּא סָבָא לָא עֲבִיד דְּמִיסְתְּכַר,
phrases.english: He said to him: The river Malka Sava does not usually get dammed up,
so it is a regional disaster;
go subtract it from him.
phrases.notes: He means: take this loss off the rent you owe the owner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling on the case just described.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An unusual blockage of the river counts as a מכת מדינה, so the renter may reduce his rent even when the rent is money.

steps.title: The רבנן challenge רבא from רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן point out that רבי יהודה says a money renter gets no discount no matter what.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said to רבא: But didn't we learn that רבי יהודה says, if he rented for money, he does not get a discount from his rent either way?
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן challenge רבא's ruling, because a משנה seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Either way" means whether or not it was a מכת מדינה. The garlic field was rented for money, so according to רבי יהודה there should be no discount at all. רבא's ruling seems to go directly against this משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Either way, whether or not there was a regional disaster
His rent (the fixed payment he owes)

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to Rava:
But didn't we learn:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אִם קִבְּלָה הֵימֶנּוּ בְּמָעוֹת –
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: If he received it from him for money,
whether this way or that way,
phrases.notes: He means whether it was a regional disaster or not.

phrases.english: he does not subtract from his rent!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's ruling from step 14 using רבי יהודה's view from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that a money renter gets a discount in a מכת מדינה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה says a money renter never gets a discount, even in a מכת מדינה. This was a money rent, so רבא's ruling seems to go against the משנה.

steps.title: רבא: no one follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the halacha does not follow רבי יהודה, so his view does not decide the case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to them: Nobody is concerned with רבי יהודה's opinion.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his ruling. רבי יהודה's view is not the accepted halacha.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not reread the משנה. He simply says that רבי יהודה's opinion is not followed. That leaves the first view of the משנה in place: in a מכת מדינה the renter gets a discount, whether he pays in crops or in money.

keyTerms.meaning: Is concerned about, takes into account
For the opinion of רבי יהודה

steps.whatToRemember: In practice, a renter gets a discount in a מכת מדינה even if his rent is money. רבי יהודה's opposite view is not followed.

phrases.english: He said to them:
There is no one who is concerned for the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pushes aside the source as a view the halacha does not follow.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה's view in the משנה should block a discount on a money rent.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since no one follows רבי יהודה, the first view of the משנה decides, and a money renter also gets a discount in a מכת מדינה.

steps.title: New משנה: paying wheat rent from the field's own wheat
steps.stepSummary: A renter who owes ten כור of wheat pays from the field's own wheat, whether it is blighted or excellent.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone rents a field for ten כור of wheat a year and the crop gets blighted, he pays the owner from that wheat. If the wheat turns out especially good, he cannot say, "I'll buy you wheat from the market instead." He must pay from the field's own wheat.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that wheat rent is paid from what this field produced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rent is tied to this field's crop. So the owner must accept poor wheat if that is what grew, and the renter must hand over excellent wheat if that is what grew. In both cases the amount stays ten כור. Only the quality follows the field.

keyTerms.meaning: One who takes a field to work for a fixed payment
It was struck, meaning the crop was blighted or damaged
From within it, from the field's own produce

steps.confusionAlert: "נוֹתֵן לוֹ מִתּוֹכָהּ" does not mean the renter pays less. He still owes the full ten כור. The משנה is only talking about which wheat he gives: the field's own, poor or good.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who receives a field from his fellow
for ten kor of wheat per year,
and it was blighted, he gives him from it.
If its wheat was fine,
he may not say to him:
I will buy from the market,
rather, he gives him from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמְקַבֵּל שָׂדֶה מֵחֲבֵירוֹ בַּעֲשָׂרָה כּוֹר חִטִּים לְשָׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a related topic: the quality of a crop rent.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fixed wheat rent is paid from the field's own produce, whether that wheat is poor or excellent.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rule the גמרא will test right away: when is the rent "tied to the field," so that it is paid from whatever grew there?

steps.title: The case of the hay field paid in barley
steps.stepSummary: A man leased land to grow hay, paying in barley. After the hay grew, he planted barley there too, and the barley was blighted.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man took land to grow hay and agreed to pay a set number of כור of barley. The field produced hay. Then he plowed it, sowed barley, and that barley got blighted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a case that is not quite like the משנה. It is setting up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the rent (wheat) is the same crop the field was leased to grow. Here the field was leased for hay but the rent was barley. The barley that got blighted was an extra crop he planted after the hay. So it is unclear whether this barley counts as the field's own produce for the rent.

keyTerms.meaning: גמרא (start of the discussion on the משנה)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
A certain man who received land for hay
for kor of barley.
phrases.notes: His rent was a set amount of barley, even though he was growing hay.

phrases.english: It produced hay,
and he plowed it and sowed it with barley,
and that barley was blighted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real case to test how far the משנה's rule reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A case is presented: land leased for hay, paid in barley, followed by a second crop of barley that was blighted.

steps.title: רב חביבא asks רבינא whether this matches the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב חביבא asks רבינא whether this case falls under "if it was blighted, he pays from it."
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חביבא from Sura on the Euphrates sent the question to רבינא: What is the law in a case like this? Is it like the משנה's "it was blighted, he pays from it," or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The question is asked: can the renter pay the owner with the blighted barley, as in the משנה? The answer will come in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the case is like the משנה, the renter may pay with the blighted barley. If not, he must pay good barley, because this barley was not really the crop the field was leased for. The גמרא is asking whether the משנה's rule stretches to this unusual setup.

keyTerms.meaning: He sent it (sent the question by message)
In a case like this, what is the law?
Is it similar to, is it compared to

phrases.english: Rav Haviva from Sura on the Euphrates sent it
before Ravina:
In a case like this, what is the law?
Is it like "it was blighted, he gives him from it,"
phrases.notes: He is quoting our משנה from step 17.

phrases.english: or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the משנה from step 17 applies to the case in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a renter who leased land for hay and paid in barley may pay with the blighted barley he later grew, as in the משנה's rule.

steps.title: רבינא: in the hay case the land did its job
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says the hay case is different from the משנה, because there the land produced what it was rented for.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Are the cases alike? There, in the משנה, the land did not do its owner's job. Here, the land did do its owner's job.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers רב חביבא's question from Step 19. He says no, the blighted-barley case is not covered by the rule in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lets the renter pay from blighted crops only when the land itself failed to produce properly. In the hay case the land grew the hay it was rented for. The barley was the renter's own extra planting, so its failure is his problem, and he must pay with good barley.

keyTerms.meaning: Are they comparable? A way of saying 'these cases are different.'
Mission, job: what the land was supposed to do

steps.whatToRemember: The renter may pay from damaged crops only when the land itself failed at the job it was rented for.
steps.whyThisMatters: This 'did the land do its owner's job?' test becomes the yardstick for the next cases too.

phrases.english: He said to him: Is it comparable?
phrases.notes: "He" is רבינא, answering רב חביבא's question from the last step.

phrases.english: There, the land did not perform
its owner's mission;
here, the land did perform
phrases.notes: "Here" is the hay case: the field grew the hay it was rented for.

phrases.english: its owner's mission.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in Step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the hay-then-barley case falls under 'if it was blighted, he pays from it.'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. The land did its job by growing the hay, so the blighted barley does not qualify.

steps.title: The orchard whose wine turned sour
steps.stepSummary: A man rented an orchard for ten barrels of wine, and the wine turned sour. רב כהנא thought this matches the משנה's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man rented an orchard from his friend for ten barrels of wine a year. That wine turned sour. רב כהנא wanted to say: this is our משנה, which says if the crop was blighted, he pays from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new real-life case. רב כהנא suggests the renter may pay with the sour wine, just like blighted crops in the משנה. This sets up רב אשי's response.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא treats sour wine like a blighted crop: the produce came out bad, so the owner should accept it. The question is whether wine going sour is really the field's failure.

keyTerms.meaning: Thought to say: a first suggestion that may be rejected
This is (the case of) our משנה

phrases.english: A certain man who received an orchard from his fellow
for ten barrels of wine,
that wine turned sour.
Rav Kahana thought to say:
This is our Mishnah:
if it was blighted, he gives him from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case testing the same rule just clarified in Step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב כהנא's first suggestion: the renter may pay with the sour wine, like blighted crops.

steps.title: רב אשי: the land did its job, so sour wine doesn't count
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rejects רב כהנא's comparison, because the grapes grew fine and only the wine went bad.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him: Are the cases alike? There, the land did not do its job. Here, the land did do its job.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes back on רב כהנא, using the same test רבינא just used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה the field itself produced bad crops. Here the orchard produced good grapes, and the wine soured later, while it was in the renter's hands. So the renter must pay with good wine.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי: מִי דָּמֵי?
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to him: Is it comparable?
There, the land did not perform its mission;
here, the land did perform its mission.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי: מִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב כהנא's comparison in Step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects applying the משנה's blighted-crop rule to sour wine.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The damage did not come from the land. The grapes were good and the wine spoiled later.

steps.title: Where רב אשי agrees: shrunken grapes and blighted sheaves
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי agrees that if the grapes themselves shrank, or the sheaves were blighted, the renter may pay from that produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אשי agrees about grapes that shrank, and about a field whose sheaves were blighted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets the limits of רב אשי's ruling: when the damage is in the crop itself, he agrees the renter may pay from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Shrunken grapes and blighted sheaves mean the land did not produce properly, so the land failed at its job. That fits the משנה's rule. The sour wine was different because the spoiling happened after a good harvest.

keyTerms.meaning: Grapes that shrank or shriveled while growing

steps.whatToRemember: Damage that comes from the land (bad crops) means the renter may pay from that produce. Damage after a good harvest (wine souring) means he must pay with good produce.

phrases.english: And Rav Ashi concedes
regarding grapes that shrank
and regarding a field that was blighted in its sheaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רב אשי's rejection in Step 22 to damage that happens after a good harvest.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: When the crop itself is damaged, the land failed at its job, and the renter may pay from the damaged produce.

steps.title: New משנה: switching which crop is planted in a rented field
steps.stepSummary: A renter who took a field for barley may not plant wheat. If he took it for wheat, he may plant barley, but רבן שמעון בן גמליאל forbids this. The same pattern holds for grain and legumes.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone rents a field to plant barley, he may not plant wheat. If he rented it for wheat, he may plant barley, but רבן שמעון בן גמליאל forbids it. If he rented it for grain, he may not plant legumes. If he rented it for legumes, he may plant grain, but רבן שמעון בן גמליאל forbids it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It discusses whether a renter may plant a different crop than the one agreed on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא allows switching only in one direction: from the crop that is harder on the field to the one that is easier, so the owner loses nothing. That is why wheat may become barley, and legumes may become grain. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל forbids any switch from what was agreed.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה: marks the start of a new משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read the משנה as allowing switching both ways. The first opinion permits only wheat to barley and legumes to grain, never the other direction.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One who receives a field from his fellow
to plant it with barley
may not plant it with wheat.
If for wheat, he may plant it with barley,
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel forbids.
If for grain, he may not plant it with legumes.
If for legumes, he may plant it with grain,
and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel forbids.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַמְקַבֵּל שָׂדֶה מֵחֲבֵירוֹ לְזׇרְעָהּ שְׂעוֹרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic: changing the crop in a rented field.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A renter may switch only to a crop that is easier on the field (wheat to barley, legumes to grain). רבן שמעון בן גמליאל forbids any switch.

steps.title: רב חסדא gives the reason for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל forbids switching crops because of the פסוק in צפניה: the remnant of Israel shall not speak lies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: What is the reason of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל? Because it is written: "The remnant of Israel shall not do wrong, nor speak lies, and a deceitful tongue shall not be found in their mouth."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה. רב חסדא asks why רבן שמעון בן גמליאל forbids planting barley in a field rented for wheat, and he answers with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Barley is less hard on the soil than wheat, so the owner does not seem to lose anything. רב חסדא explains that this is not about loss. The renter said "wheat," and going back on what you said is a kind of falsehood, which the פסוק forbids.

keyTerms.meaning: The remnant of Israel (the Jewish people)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the idea that a person must keep his word even when changing it hurts no one. The next steps test this idea.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Chisda said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel?
As it is written: "The remnant of Israel shall not do iniquity,
nor speak lies,
neither shall a deceitful tongue be found in their mouth."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's opinion in the משנה from Step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל forbids changing from the agreed crop because going back on one's word is falsehood, even without any loss to the owner.

steps.title: A challenge begins from the Purim collection for the poor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: money collected for פורים must be used for פורים, and a poor person may not even buy a sandal strap with it unless he made a condition. That is רבי מאיר's view. The ברייתא then turns to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, whose words continue on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: The Purim collection is for Purim, but we are not too exact about it. A poor person may not buy even a strap for his sandal from it, unless he made a condition in front of the people of the city. These are the words of רבי יעקב, who said it in the name of רבי מאיר. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge to רב חסדא by quoting a ברייתא about money given for פורים. The key part, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's opinion, comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי מאיר, money given for one purpose, Purim, must stay with that purpose. Using it for something else needs a clear condition. The ברייתא is about to give רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's opinion on changing the purpose of money. The גמרא will compare that to his strictness about switching crops.

keyTerms.meaning: Money collected for the poor for Purim
In the presence of the townspeople

steps.confusionAlert: This step is not finished yet. The challenge only becomes clear once רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's words appear on the next amud.

phrases.english: They raised an objection: The Purim collection is for Purim,
and we are not exacting in the matter.
phrases.notes: He means we don't limit the poor man to exactly what his Purim meal costs.

phrases.english: And the poor person is not permitted
to buy from it a strap for his sandal,
unless he stipulated
in the presence of the people of the city,
these are the words of Rabbi Yaakov
who said it in the name of Rabbi Meir.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a challenge against רב חסדא's explanation in Step 25, using a ברייתא about changing the purpose of money.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's explanation that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds one may not change from what was agreed (Step 25).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא is about to give רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view on using פורים money for another purpose. The גמרא will set that view against his strictness about switching crops. The full contrast appears on the next amud.
